feat.name: Protected
entries: You have someone or something guarding you for as long as you can remember, even if you don't know why. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Luck Points
entries: You have a number of Luck Points equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and can spend the points on the benefits below. You regain your expended Luck Points when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Reroll
entries: Whenever you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and roll 9 or lower on the {@dice d20}, you can spend 1 Luck Point to reroll the {@dice d20}. You must accept the second result.

entries.name: Stabilize
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can spend 1 Luck Point to drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

feat.name: Nocturnal
entries: You have spent many formative years in the darkness of night. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@spell Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. If you already have {@spell Darkvision|XPHB}, its range increases by 30 feet.

entries.name: Slink in Shadows
entries: Whenever you make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check while in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the {@dice d20} as a 10.

feat.name: Healthy
entries: You have, for whatever reason, maintained a physically healthy lifestyle. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Hit Die Use
entries: The first time you would spend a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} after completing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you gain the benefit of spending the Hit Die but do not spend it.

entries.name: Saving Throw Proficiency
entries: Choose one ability in which you lack saving throw proficiency. You gain saving throw proficiency with the chosen ability.

feat.name: Well-Read
entries: You grew up with your nose buried in books. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Creature Lore
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can recall lore about a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself; you know one {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, {@spell Resistance|XPHB}, {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB}, or Trait of that creature. You decide when you use this ability.

entries.name: Font of Useful Knowledge
entries: When you roll a 1 on an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB}) check, you can reroll the die, and you must use the new roll.

entries.name: Rare Knowledge
entries: If you succeed on an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB}) check, you learn additional lore. The GM has final say on what you learn, if anything. The lore might consist of important details, amusing revelations, or even secret lore that has never been widely known. The more information you already know about the thing, the more precise and detailed the information you receive is. That information is accurate but might be couched in figurative language or poetry, as determined by the GM.

feat.name: Alacrity
entries: You move at supernatural speeds. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Burst of Speed
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 1 Blood Point to gain an additional action. That action can be used to take only the {@action Attack|XPHB} (one attack only) or {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Fast
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls.

feat.name: Cloak of Shadows
entries: You are adept at supernaturally masking your presence. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Enshrouded
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your next Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check on the current turn.

entries.name: Unseen Passage
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

You can use this {@action Magic|XPHB} action a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Convincing Thoughts
entries: Your supernatural powers of persuasion are uncannily hidden from your victim's mind. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Charming Smile
entries: You can cast the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Rationalize
entries: When spells or effects that cause the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition end, the target doesn't know it was {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you.

feat.name: Daywalker
entries: The sun's light doesn't harm you as badly as it does other Kindred. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Dhampir's Boon
entries: When you take damage from sunlight, reduce the damage taken by 2.

entries.name: Endure Radiance
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 1 Blood Point to remove your {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage for 1 minute.

entries.name: Wake with Evening's Freshness
entries: When you start a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you count as having at least 1 Blood Point for that {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Animalism)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} and {@skill Nature|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Auspex)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Investigation|XPHB} and {@skill Perception|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Celerity)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain an extra {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, which you can use with any of your existing {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Dominate)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Deception|XPHB} and {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Fortitude)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
{@variantrule Damage|XPHB} dealt to you except Fire and Radiant is reduced by an amount equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Obfuscate)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} and {@skill Stealth|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Oblivion)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You can see normally in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}—both magical and nonmagical—within 90 feet of yourself.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Potence)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

When you hit a creature with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can deal extra damage to the target equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Presence)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance|XPHB} and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} skills. If you already have proficiency in that skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

feat.name: Discipline Acquisition (Protean)
entries: You learn the basic concepts of a vampiric Discipline from another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You can deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage to a target you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

feat.name: Feral Whispers
entries: You have an animalistic connection to the creatures of the wilderness. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Call of the Wild
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 1 Blood Point to summon a number of Large or smaller Beasts (such as a {@creature Rat|XMM} or {@creature Wolf|XMM}) equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). The total {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} for summoned Beasts can't exceed your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. A summoned Beast arrives at your location in {@dice 1d4 + 1} rounds and is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you for 1 minute after it arrives. In combat, a Beast shares your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

entries.name: Shared Spirit
entries: You can cast the {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} spell, but only as a {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB}.

feat.name: Forceful Presence
entries: You can focus your vampiric presence to instill emotions in others. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Awe
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Performance|XPHB}, and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks for 10 minutes.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Daunt
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check and choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to the result of your {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} check. On a failed save, the creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower automatically succeeds on its saving throw against this effect.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Animalism)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.

You can cast the {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} and {@spell Animal Messenger|XPHB} spells but only as Rituals. You can cast the {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Auspex)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 1 Blood Point to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence and Wisdom checks and saving throws for 1 minute.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Celerity)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} or as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you are hit by an attack roll, you can expend 1 Blood Point to double your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and gain a +3 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Dominate)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.

You can cast the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} and {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} spells. You can cast either spell without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Fortitude)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.

When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feat if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Obfuscate)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.
While entirely in {@spell Darkness|XPHB}, you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition to any creature that relies on {@spell Darkvision|XPHB} to see you in that {@spell Darkness|XPHB}.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Oblivion)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.
You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Darkness|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Potence)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 2 Blood Points to empower your strikes for 1 minute. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Force damage. In addition, you deal double damage to objects and structures.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Presence)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.

You expend 3 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Fear|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}, and creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw against the spell.

feat.name: Greater Discipline Acquisition (Protean)
entries: Your talents with the vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline have improved. You gain the following benefits.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 2 Blood Points to deal an extra {@damage 2d6} Slashing damage to a target you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} for 1 minute.

feat.name: Hardened Skin
entries: Your skin is dense and difficult to damage. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Damage Resistance
entries: Select Bludgeoning or Slashing damage. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the chosen damage.

feat.name: Heightened Senses
entries: Your vampiric senses are stronger and more precise than ever before. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Preternatural Perception
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB} and {@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Sense the Unseen
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet. In addition, you can cast the {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: The Kiss
entries: Your bite is intoxicating to your prey.

entries.name: Pleasurable Feeding
entries: When you feed, you can choose to roll d4s instead of d6s for your Feed Dice. When you do so, you regain 1 Blood Point on a roll of a 4 on the {@dice d4}, and the creature is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you. The {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition lasts until the end of your next turn.

feat.name: Lethal Body
entries: You possess potent vampiric strength, turning your bare hands into deadly weapons.

entries.name: Crushing Blows
entries: You can deal {@damage 1d8} extra damage when you hit a target with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. The extra damage is the same type dealt by that strike.

entries.name: Iron Grip
entries: A creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saving throws to escape your grapple.

feat.name: Loyal Servant
entries: You have a loyal companion who has gained power from your blood. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Companion
entries: A loyal Beast or Humanoid is Blood Bound to you. {@filter Choose a Beast or Humanoid stat block|bestiary|Challenge Rating=[&0;&3]|type=beast;humanoid} that has a maximum {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} of up to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. When choosing a companion, you may look in the monster section of source books or elsewhere for an eligible Beast or Humanoid if the Game Master permits you to do so.

entries.name: Power in the Blood
entries: Your Loyal Servant has one {@filter Kindred feat|feats|category=kf|level=level 1;level 2} of your choice, and it counts as a level 2 Kindred for the purpose of selecting a Kindred feat. In addition, your Loyal Servant can spend 1 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} in place of 1 Blood Point for the purpose of its feat.

entries.name: Replacing a Servant
entries: If your servant is killed or otherwise leaves, you can choose a new Loyal Servant after 30 days. The GM can lengthen or shorten this time based on in-game circumstances.

entries.name: The Blood Bond
entries: While Blood Bound to a Kindred, a creature is considered {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by that Kindred and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid being {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} by other creatures. This is in addition to the effects from the {@item Kindred Vitae|BoundByBlood} consumable.

A Blood Bond can be suppressed for 1 minute if the creature succeeds on a DC 25 Charisma saving throw. The bond is only permanently removed if the creature doesn't drink from that Kindred again for a year, or if the Kindred in question is killed.

feat.name: Mind Tricks
entries: You can dominate others with your mental powers. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cloud Memory
entries: You can cast the {@spell Command|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. In addition, you gain access to a special command.

entries.name: Forget
entries: The target has only a hazy and unsure recollection of the last 5 minutes.

feat.name: Self-Control
entries: You manage your Beast better than many. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Reining the Beast
entries: When you would be affected by the {@classFeature The Beast|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1||Hunger} of your Beast feature, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to immediately end the effect.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Animalism)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.

You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Charm Monster|XPHB} or {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw against the spell.

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Auspex)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.

You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} but only as a ritual. You can cast {@spell Clairvoyance|XPHB} and {@spell Telepathy|XPHB}. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either spell in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Celerity)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 1 Blood Point to gain an additional action. That action can be used to take only the {@action Attack|XPHB} (one attack only), {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, {@action Dodge|XPHB}, {@action Hide|XPHB}, or {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Dominate)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.

You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Mass Suggestion|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw against the spell.

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Fortitude)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.

When you take damage except Fire and Radiant, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage taken by your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} plus your Constitution modifier (minimum reduction of 1).

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Obfuscate)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.

You can cast the {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. In addition, when you gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, you can expend up to 3 Blood Points to grant up to three other creatures that you can see within 30 feet of yourself the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. The number of Blood Points expended in this way equals the number of creatures affected by this feat.

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Oblivion)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.

You can expend 2 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Evard's Black Tentacles|XPHB|Black Tentacles} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, the {@spell Evard's Black Tentacles|XPHB|Black Tentacles} deal {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage and {@damage 2d6} Cold damage (instead of {@damage 3d6} Bludgeoning damage).

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Potence)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend up to 6 Blood Points to increase your Strength score by an amount equal to the number of Blood Points expended in this way for 1 hour.

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Presence)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.
You can cast the {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot.

feat.name: Superior Discipline Acquisition (Protean)
entries: The vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline is now second nature to you. You gain the following benefits.

You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Meld into Stone|XPHB} spell on yourself. When you cast the spell in this way, the object or surface must be dirt, sand, or clay, and the spell's duration becomes 24 hours for that casting.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Animalism)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

You cast the {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB} spell as its level 7 version without expending a spell slot, and you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. Once you cast the spell with this feat, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Auspex)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.
You can expend 2 Blood Points to cast the {@spell True Seeing|XPHB} spell on yourself.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Celerity)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

You can expend 2 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Haste|XPHB} spell on yourself. When you cast the spell in this way, when the spell ends, you aren't {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} isn't reduced to 0.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Dominate)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

You cast the {@spell Dominate Person|XPHB} spell as its level 7 version without expending a spell slot, and you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. Once you cast the spell with this feat, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Fortitude)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

When you take damage except Fire and Radiant, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 2 Blood Points to reduce the damage you take by half (round down) or 4 Blood Points to reduce the damage to 0.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Obfuscate)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the {@spell Greater Invisibility|XPHB} spell. When you cast the spell in this way, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Oblivion)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

When a creature that you can see within 10 feet of you misses an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 1 Blood Point to deal {@damage 2d8} Bludgeoning damage and {@damage 2d8} Cold damage to that creature.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Potence)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 2 Blood Points to give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls using Strength for 1 minute. In addition, whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll using Strength, you can reroll one of the dice once.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Presence)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast the {@spell Sanctuary|XPHB} spell on yourself. When you cast the spell in this way, the spell doesn't end if you make an attack roll, cast a spell, or deal damage.

feat.name: Supreme Discipline Acquisition (Protean)
entries: You have learned all you can about a vampiric Discipline of another clan or bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} on yourself, shape-shifting into a {@creature Bat|XMM}, {@creature Cat|XMM}, {@creature Rat|XMM}, {@creature Raven|XMM}, or {@creature Wolf|XMM}. You can expend 1 additional Blood Point to shape-shift into a {@creature Dire Wolf|XMM}, {@creature Giant Bat|XMM}, {@creature Giant Rat|XMM}, or {@creature Panther|XMM}. While in that form, you retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores.

feat.name: Touch of Darkness
entries: There is darkness within you, and it has given you a gift. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Eyes of Night
entries: You can see normally in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}—both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet of yourself.

entries.name: Shadowplay
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

feat.name: Vitae Concentration
entries: Your body is more efficient at holding and processing vitae. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Increase Blood Pool
entries: Your Blood Point maximum increases by your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

feat.name: Boon of Generations
entries: You have become the embodiment of the ancient vampires of your bloodline. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Deep Feeding
entries: Whenever you roll a Feed Die for your {@classFeature Feed|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1} feature, you can reroll the die if it rolls a 1, and you must use the new roll.

entries.name: Potent Blood
entries: Your Blood Point maximum increases by 5.

feat.name: Thin-Blooded

otherSummary.entry: Can Be Chosen in Place of Any Origin Feat

entries: You have a portion of a vampire's blood flowing in your veins. You are a thin-blood, often destined for a place among the clanless. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Able to Feed
entries: You feed on the blood of other creatures. This is most often accomplished through your sharp fangs. As an action, you can feed on another creature within 5 feet of yourself if the target is willing, {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you, or has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, or {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. You can feed only once per turn.

You have {@dice 2d6} Feed Dice. When you feed, roll up to your maximum Feed Dice plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1). The creature takes Necrotic damage equal to the roll's total. This damage only reduces the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum by an amount equal to the roll's total. If you roll a 6 on a {@dice d6} on a Feed Die, you can regain 1 expended Blood Point. If a creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced to 0, you can regain 1 expended Blood Point.

entries.name: Feeding from the Willing
entries: If you feed on a willing creature or a creature {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you, it can spend 1 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die}. It rolls the {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} and reduces its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum by the amount rolled, and you can regain 1 expended Blood Point. Feeding in this way doesn't end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Hit Die Deficit
entries: If a creature has no remaining {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Feed Dice plus your Constitution modifier, and the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the roll's total.

entries.name: Maximum Successful Feedings
entries: A creature can provide a number of Blood Points based on its size. A Small creature provides 1 Blood Point, a Medium provides 3, a Large provides 5, a Huge provides 7, and a Gargantuan provides 10. A creature regains all lost Blood Points when it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Creature Susceptible to Feed
entries: You can feed on any creature with blood or other life-giving fluid. Work with your GM to determine the types of creatures you can feed on.

entries.name: Kindred, but Not Kindred
entries: You ignore the Kindred class prerequisite for choosing {@filter Kindred feats|feats|category=kf}. You can't gain levels in the Kindred class.

entries.name: Kindred Vitae
entries: You have a number of Blood Points equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} minus one.

entries.name: Supernatural Spellcasting
entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for spells from your Kindred feats. Your spells require no Verbal or Somatic components, and they require no Material components unless they are consumed by the spell or have a cost specified in it. Taking damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} for spells cast using this feature.

variantrule.name: Masquerade Level
entries: It is easier for {@class Kindred|BoundByBlood} to survive amongst humanity when mortals don't suspect there are monsters in their midst. As a {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} adventure progresses, there are encounters and scenes that can be made more or less difficult based on the Masquerade Level, a measure of how wary the local populace is toward the possibility of monsters lurking in the night.
There are six Masquerade Levels (listed in ascending order): Superstition, Disbelief, Skepticism, Concern, Wariness, and Alarm.

items: {@b Superstition}. Most people don't believe in vampires or other monstrous creatures and dimiss such stories.
{@b Disbelief}. A few people believe vampires exist, but they are ignored or thought ill.
{@b Skepticism}. There are rampant rumors about strange happenings, but most events are dismissed with the right application of logic.
{@b Concern}. Too many unexplained events and circumstances have everyone asking questions. People are beginning to investigate.
{@b Wariness}. People know the night is dangerous, and they often lock themselves inside at dusk or form patrols.
{@b Alarm}. Monsters are real, and humanity must hunt them!

entries: Most adventures begin at the Superstition level. There are choices the characters can make that prompt the Storyteller to raise or lower the Masquerade Level. Apart from localized effects detailed in each section, some encounters are altered when the Masquerade Level reaches certain points. The use of Masquerade Level helps the Storyteller create a more realistic environmental response to Kindred characters who are making careless or foolish choices as the story progresses.

variantrule.name: Narrated Feeding
entries: Kindred must drink blood to survive; it's that hunger that drives them and creates dramatic tension in the narrative. For {@class Kindred|BoundByBlood} characters, feeding can be made part of—or the reason for—additional combat encounters. An adventure where one or more characters are Kindred will likely call for feeding outside of planned encounters. When playing {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} using fifth edition rules, unnecessary combat can slow the game. To help alleviate this, the Storyteller can occasionally use these rules for Narrated Feeding.

Instead of requiring an entire combat encounter, Narrated Feeding allows the Storyteller to give characters the chance to perform their necessary feeding "off camera" with a single skill check. The skill a Kindred decides to use varies based on the style of feeding the character is attempting, and the DC of the check is based upon the environment in which the feeding attempt is being made, as shown on the table {@area below|135|x}.

items.name: Hunting Grounds

If a Narrated Feeding attempt succeeds, the Kindred can roll its Feed Dice to determine how many Blood Points it regains. No matter the result of the roll, the Kindred regains a minimum of 1 Blood Point.

If a Narrated Feeding attempt fails, the Kindred doesn't gain a Blood Point and the Storyteller can decide if the situation warrants greater penalties, such as gaining 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} or increasing the {@variantrule Masquerade Level|BoundByBlood}.

entries.name: A World of Darkness
entries: You are already intimately familiar with our world. The sun rises, the sun sets, and, in between, people go about the business of living. Most of them never look too closely at what moves in the dark. The World of Darkness is a mirror of our world, our history, our cities. The horror of what you see in this mirror lives in the margins of the familiar.

Here, vampires have walked among humanity since before recorded history, moving through every age and empire, every era of plague and plenty. They are not a modern invention but an ancient entity, a continuous secret underpinning civilization as a whole.
That secret sounds rather different depending on the century.

In the Dark Ages, the world was lit only by fire. Most of Europe was forest. Old Roman roads cut through it in straight lines that represented a distant civilization's expression of confidence. Outside the cities, the landscape is largely unmapped and ungoverned, full of things that have not yet been named and are certainly not waiting to be. It is a world of faith and superstition, of feudal courts and a wilderness that starts twenty yards past the last hut in the hamlet and does not end in any particular location.

This is the world of {@i Vampire: The Dark Ages}, and the setting of the included adventure "{@book One Last Goodbye|BoundByBlood|2}." It is a fundamentally different world for vampires to inhabit than the modern nights their descendants will eventually learn to navigate. The political machinery that defines later vampiric society gets built here. Right now, it is still very raw.

In the modern era, vampires maintain what they call the Masquerade: a centuries-old tradition of concealment, a collective agreement to stay invisible to a mortal population that would destroy them if it truly believed. Vampires in the modern world exist inside that agreement, are shaped by it, constrained by it.

The Masquerade does not exist yet in the Dark Ages. Its foundation is still being built. Vampires have not yet collectively codified how they will interface with mortal civilization. Every peasant already believes in demons. The monstrous man in the castle who has not aged since the lord's father was a boy is, to the village below, a basic fact of local life. The stakes of discovery are real, but faith does the work that secrecy will later have to do, and faith is much less precise. A vampire lord can be exposed by a suspicious priest or a child who saw the wrong thing at the wrong hour. The game of concealment is messier, more immediate, and more personal.

entries.name: Vampire and D&D
entries: Games like {@i Vampire}, set within the World of Darkness, are built on the Storyteller system, a ruleset designed around collaborative narrative and moral complexity. Combat is certainly present, but it is not the engine. This system does what its name promises.

D&D is a different kind of game. It often utilizes maps, miniatures, structured encounters, and tactical combat as parts of its core pleasures. Adventures are built around objectives pursued through dangerous terrain, confrontations that play out in initiative order, and a party that solves problems by moving through space together. Adaptations of the World of Darkness to other systems are not unprecedented. GURPS produced {@i World of Darkness} supplements in the 1990s, and the lesson those adaptations demonstrated holds here: when you have a great setting, different systems simply open different doors into it.

What the 5E format offers a Kindred party is tactical weight. The dungeon is sometimes literally a dungeon. The rival is something you have to fight through a burning building to reach. The wilderness has teeth and the map ends before the danger does.

Nosferatu moving through tunnels beneath a dying city, carrying information three factions will kill to possess. Gangrel tracking rivals through wilderness, far past the last torch on the road. Ventrue navigating a court where the mortal prince is someone else's pawn and the negotiation was designed to fail. A coterie arriving at a remote village where something has been feeding, and strong indication that the locals have already decided it must be them.

entries.name: Wooden Stake (1 SP)
entries: {@i Simple Weapon}

While any modest length of sharpened wood can be used as an improvised weapon, wooden stakes that have been carved, treated, and fire-hardened are specifically useful against Kindred. Dedicated wooden stakes use the weapon profile below.

entries.name: Driving the Stake
entries: If you are within 5 feet of a Kindred with the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} or {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, you can take an action to make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the wooden stake is driven into the heart of the Kindred.

entries.name: Silver Weapons and Ammunition
entries: Silver isn't an ideal material from which to craft edged weapons, but it possesses innate traits that pose a threat to certain supernatural creatures. Use the {@area Silver Weapons|11g|x} and {@area Silver Ammunition|11h|x} tables statistics of weapons made with silver blades, points, or flanges.

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a {@dc 10} Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wooden Weapons and Ammunition
entries: Whether due to a tool or implement being wielded in a hurry, or the active knowledge of someone who understands the intrinsic weakness of Kindred, a weapon made solely of wood can pierce the heart. Use the {@area Wooden Weapons|121a|x} and {@area Wooden Ammunition|121b|x} tables for statistics of piercing weapons made with wooden points, or ranged weapons firing wooden ammunition.

entries.name: Wooden Melee Weapons

data.name: Appendix A: Bestiary
entries: This appendix provides stat blocks for creatures that characters may encounter in the {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} setting. The following stat blocks are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Highland Wolf
entries: Large packs of wolves hunt across the highlands, rarely choosing to interact with humans. When food becomes scarce or when travelers become separated from their groups, these thickly furred canines become a deadly threat.

entries.name: Lupine
entries: Werewolves, or what Kindred call the lupines, are another powerful denizen of the supernatural world. Lupines are overwhelmingly strong, terrifyingly fast, immensely resilient, and have held a frenzied level of hatred for the Kindred for as long as either side can remember. When one is not taking the shape of a human or a wolf, it stands on two legs to become a ten-foot-tall killing machine of fur, claws, and fangs who can split stone with a single slash and endure horrific amounts of damage. A single lupine is more than a match for a group of younger Kindred, and even powerful Kindred are wise to give pause before engaging unprepared.

entries.name: Monster Hunter
entries: Armed with a variety of skills, tools, and beliefs, the monster hunter pursues supernatural threats wherever they hide. Whether a hunter knows real lore or just superstitious stories about the Kindred doesn't make the hunter any less deadly.

entries.name: Trapper
entries: A skilled hunter and survivalist who makes a living trapping and skinning animals in the wilderness. They effectively spread traps around them when ambushing prey.

entries.name: Villager
entries: The common people of the village are generally useful to Kindred as a source to subtly feed upon. When afraid or angry enough to fight, a villager can be quite dangerous, especially in groups.

entries.name: Villager Militia
entries: These brave folk take up arms to defend their village against bandits, invaders, and sometimes beasts lurking in their midst.

data.name: One Last Goodbye
entries: A {@i Vampire: The Dark Ages} Adventure Compatible with 5.5e Rules for Level 4 Characters by Bryan C.P. Steele

There is a world hidden from humanity that survives in the space between superstition and disbelief. This shadowed world of secrets exists alongside the mortal world and has for tens of thousands of years. The denizens of this dark world prey upon humanity while desperately clinging to what was once mortal inside themselves.

It is a World of Darkness in which the monsters that go bump in the night are all too real, and you can become one of these supernatural creatures. You can become a Kindred, or, as they are more commonly known in folklore ... vampires.

entries.name: Kindred and the Greater World of Darkness
entries: Vampires exist. In modern times, they call themselves Kindred. They have survived in secret since biblical times, drinking blood to maintain their existence and sate the eternal hunger of the Beast that rages within.

In the Dark Ages, the time when this adventure is set, vampires more commonly call themselves Cainites, tracing their lineage to Caine, who was often cited as the first of their kind. However, there are varied legends of where and how the first vampire came into being, and surely the truth lies somewhere between them all.

As their name implies, Kindred draw their lineages back to a small assortment of original bloodlines from which they all stem. These ancient bloodlines, called clans by the Kindred, create a familial bond that helps shape each into something both unique and familiar to others who share that lineage.

Over millennia, the Kindred of each clan found others to share their immortal curse with. Many times, these new additions to the bloodlines were chosen for similar interests, beliefs, or personal connections, and no matter how far removed from their original vampiric roots, something in their blood remembered. With the addition of new generations of ageless Kindred created by the last, the clans progressed through time. They are powerful in the sense that they can perform wondrous and unexplainable feats of the supernatural, but with that power comes an endless and sinister price to pay—the Beast.

Each Kindred fights the eternal hunger for blood. At all times, the Beast claws within their motionless hearts, urging them to feral violence and the need to sate a thirst that often goes beyond the simple need for sustenance. The stronger the Beast becomes, the farther Kindred pull away from what made them human. As the years, decades, and even centuries pass, it becomes harder for Kindred to remember what it is like to be mortal, to see humans as relationships instead of nourishment. When Kindred lose their grip on what it is to be human, the Beast takes the reins, and a frenzy of bottled-up monstrosity erupts. Most forge mental and emotional anchors, called Touchstones, to keep them grounded in their humanity with the passage of time. It is the dichotomy of their curse—the need to exist alongside and within the realm of humanity, but to forever battle the urge to consume it.

Even with the vampiric powers lurking within their blood, Kindred learn early in their existence about their weaknesses. The merciless touch of fire and sunlight. The instant paralysis of wood through the heart. The entropic decline of going without feeding. These are real threats to a Kindred's existence, but nothing can compare to their truest foe—the atrocities that spring from humanity's uncaged fears. Humans fear what they don't understand, and they often destroy what they fear. This fact, combined with their vast numbers, forces the Kindred to maintain a clandestine Masquerade to keep their existence a secret from the mortal world. They wear their figurative masks, walk amongst humanity, and do their best to avoid revealing their existence. If humanity ever really believed vampires were hidden among them, they would go to extreme lengths to wipe the Kindred out. This is why the Kindred set rules and traditions for themselves and those they create; what good is supernatural strength, telepathic dominance, or marble-hard flesh when hundreds of incensed and afraid mortals descend upon you while you sleep?

Where we find the Kindred, we find fractured souls trying to stave off the eventual fall to their Beast's monstrous instincts, all while doing their best to be a part of the secret World of Darkness that envelopes their existence. The question all Kindred must ask themselves is: Can I indulge the monster within without letting it be what defines me?

entries.name: Terms Frequently Used in Vampire: The Masquerade
entries: The following are specific terms used by Kindred in the {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} setting. They might appear in this adventure or be used in dialogue.

items.name: Beast, The
items.entry: The instinctual urges that allow a vampire's hunger to unleash a ravening monster.

items.name: Blood Bond
items.entry: A supernatural power that is held over an individual who has imbibed the vitae of a particular vampire three or more times.

items.name: Cainite
items.entry: During the Dark Ages, vampires commonly referred to themselves using this term.

items.name: Childe
items.entry: The term used to describe a vampire's offspring made by turning a mortal. The plural of which is childer.

items.name: Clan
items.entry: A group of vampires who share common characteristics passed through their vampiric bloodline.

items.name: Coterie
items.entry: A small group of Kindred who assist, support, and understand each other, often through common interests.

items.name: Discipline
items.entry: The collective term for vampiric abilities.

items.name: Domain
items.entry: A territory over which a Kindred claims control.

items.name: Embrace, The
items.entry: The process by which one Kindred turns a mortal into a Kindred. The Embrace requires a living creature to be drained of its blood and replaced with any amount of Kindred vitae.

items.name: Final Death
items.entry: When a vampire is destroyed completely.

items.name: Ghoul
items.entry: A mortal servant created by gifting vampiric blood to a living creature without draining its blood first (avoiding the Embrace).

items.name: Haven
items.entry: The physical place a vampire slumbers during the day

items.name: Hunger, The
items.entry: The all-encompassing urge to gorge blood that a vampire must constantly overcome.

items.name: Kindred
items.entry: Vampires of the modern age typically refer to themselves using this term.

items.name: Kine
items.entry: A clinical or vulgar term for humans who serve only as food.

items.name: Lupine
items.entry: The vampire term for werewolves, their fearsome mortal enemies.

items.name: Masquerade, The
items.entry: The traditional vampiric practice of hiding the existence of vampires, and other supernatural entities, from humanity, particularly by avoiding creating proof of anything supernatural.

items.name: Retainer
items.entry: A mortal creature willingly or unknowingly used as a controlled resource by a Kindred.

items.name: Sire
items.entry: The term used for the vampire who Embraced a mortal, gifting vampiric ascension.

items.name: Thrall
items.entry: A creature placed in servitude of a Kindred, often through a Blood Bond or other supernatural coercion.

items.name: Torpor
items.entry: A paralytic, deathlike state Kindred assume when they have suffered too much damage, gone without blood for too long, or both.

items.name: Touchstone
items.entry: A person, place, or object that is meaningful to vampires and reminds them of their humanity. It is a major emotional event when a Touchstone is endangered or destroyed.

items.name: Vitae
items.entry: The vampiric term for Kindred blood.

entries.name: Getting Started
entries: To play through the events of the of {@i One Last Goodbye}, a few important things must be addressed:

items: {@b The Storyteller}. The term "GM" typically refers to the person running the background and rules elements of the adventure. In {@i Vampire: The Masquerade}, this role is referred to as "The Storyteller" to help players see the game as a narrative experience instead of a set of obstacles to overcome or interactions to be "gamed." In this or any other product involved with the greater World of Darkness, any references to GM, Game Master, or Storyteller are interchangeable.

{@b Kindred Needs}. It is highly encouraged for the Storyteller running a {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} adventure to become familiar with the specific needs and requirements of {@class Kindred|BoundByBlood} characters, such as feeding rules, finding places to avoid daylight, and the mechanics of Blood Points, which are important aspects of Kindred existence.

{@b The Masquerade}. Kindred live a hidden, dangerous existence in the {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} setting. They survive in secret by avoiding encounters that could attract attention to themselves, using stealth, guile, and manipulation to keep their supernatural nature from being revealed. Kindred are quite formidable in a violent encounter; however, it is sometimes better for them to err on the side of maintaining the Masquerade.

{@b Time Period}. Many {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} and World of Darkness products take place in a modern era, but the timelessness of Kindred allows for older periods to be compelling backdrops. For example, {@i One Last Goodbye} takes place in the Dark Ages, a time when superstition and folklore carry much more weight amongst humanity.

{@b The Characters}. In {@i One Last Goodbye}, the adventure is based around a small coterie of Kindred who have known each other long enough to travel together across Britannia and Northern Europe. These are best represented by four to five characters with 4 levels in the {@class Kindred|BoundByBlood}. This allows every member of the coterie to choose their subclass and have the skills needed to experience the adventure as written.

entries.name: Additional Rules for One Last Goodbye
entries: Apart from the Storyteller needing to fully understand how the {@class Kindred|BoundByBlood} functions and reading the adventure fully to understand what events may or may not transpire, there are two additional rules in effect for {@i One Last Goodbye}, detailed as follows.

entries.name: Masquerade Level
entries: It is easier for {@class Kindred|BoundByBlood} to survive amongst humanity when mortals don't suspect there are monsters in their midst. As a {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} adventure progresses, there are encounters and scenes that can be made more or less difficult based on the Masquerade Level, a measure of how wary the local populace is toward the possibility of monsters lurking in the night.
There are six Masquerade Levels (listed in ascending order): Superstition, Disbelief, Skepticism, Concern, Wariness, and Alarm.

items: {@b Superstition}. Most people don't believe in vampires or other monstrous creatures and dimiss such stories.
{@b Disbelief}. A few people believe vampires exist, but they are ignored or thought ill.
{@b Skepticism}. There are rampant rumors about strange happenings, but most events are dismissed with the right application of logic.
{@b Concern}. Too many unexplained events and circumstances have everyone asking questions. People are beginning to investigate.
{@b Wariness}. People know the night is dangerous, and they often lock themselves inside at dusk or form patrols.
{@b Alarm}. Monsters are real, and humanity must hunt them!

entries: Most adventures begin at the Superstition level. There are choices the characters can make that prompt the Storyteller to raise or lower the Masquerade Level. Apart from localized effects detailed in each section, some encounters are altered when the Masquerade Level reaches certain points. The use of Masquerade Level helps the Storyteller create a more realistic environmental response to Kindred characters who are making careless or foolish choices as the story progresses.

entries.name: Narrated Feeding
entries: Kindred must drink blood to survive; it's that hunger that drives them and creates dramatic tension in the narrative. For {@class Kindred|BoundByBlood} characters, feeding can be made part of—or the reason for—additional combat encounters. An adventure where one or more characters are Kindred will likely call for feeding outside of planned encounters. When playing {@i Vampire: The Masquerade} using fifth edition rules, unnecessary combat can slow the game. To help alleviate this, the Storyteller can occasionally use these rules for Narrated Feeding.

Instead of requiring an entire combat encounter, Narrated Feeding allows the Storyteller to give characters the chance to perform their necessary feeding "off camera" with a single skill check. The skill a Kindred decides to use varies based on the style of feeding the character is attempting, and the DC of the check is based upon the environment in which the feeding attempt is being made, as shown on the table {@area below|135|x}.

If a Narrated Feeding attempt succeeds, the Kindred can roll its Feed Dice to determine how many Blood Points it regains. No matter the result of the roll, the Kindred regains a minimum of 1 Blood Point.
